newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly lower on weak cash.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly lower on weak cash.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly lower on Wednesday, taking cues from soybeans, with weak cash demand weighing on nearbys, traders said.
"We're feeling the effects of last week's crush," a trader said. "We got all excited last week when it came in on the high side. Now we're seeing there was no outlet."

Cash soymeal basis levels fell $6 to $8 a ton on Wednesday. Brokers said end-users were reluctant to buy old crop supplies when less expensive, abundant new crop soymeal would be available in a few weeks.

Traders said there was talk on the floor that some midday weather updates showed meteorologists were increasing rain forecasts for this weekend. But sources said most forecasters left only scattered showers in the outlook.

The August contracts were also hit by long liquidation ahead of first notice day on Thursday. Funds typically exit positions ahead of first notice day, traders said. The market was expecting heavy soyoil deliveries but no meal deliveries.
Soymeal ended $2.40 per ton lower to $0.20 higher with August down $2.40 at $253.90 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.42 to 0.30 cent per lb lower with August down 0.40 at 21.87 cents a lb.

On the day, commercials were active on both sides of the soymeal market. Cargill Inc bought 500 August and 200 each September and October but sold 200 each August and December and 100 October, traders said. Continental Grain bought 500 December while Tenco Inc sold 600 August.
ADM spread 600 August/December at $42 to $43, premium August and Continental Grain spread 300 October/December, floor sources said.
ADM, Smith Barney, Payne Webber and E.D. and F. Man International were said to be crush spreaders.

In soyoil, Produce Grain bought 300 September and 400 December, Cargill Inc bought 400 December and sold 200 December and Lee B. Stern sold 500 September and 200 each August and October, traders said.
ADM spread 300 August/September at 0.19 cent, premium September.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 34,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's volume of 33,177. Soyoil volume was pegged at 27,000 lots, against 32,721 lots.
